name: The Woman Who Comes Back
beat: A wronged woman returns from death for her due
roots: Pontianak (Malay); Oiwa, Yotsuya Kaidan (Japanese, 1825); La Llorona (Mexican); Okiku, Banchō Sarayashiki (Japanese)

name: The House Remembers
beat: A place holds the wrong done in it
roots: Pliny the Younger's haunted house at Athens, Letters 7.27 (Roman); Okiku's well (Japanese)

name: The Inherited Curse
beat: A wrong done long ago lands on you
roots: Mahsuri's curse on Langkawi (Malay); the House of Atreus (Greek)

name: The Thing You Took Home
beat: A cursed object carries the harm
roots: Pandora's jar (Greek); tsukumogami, objects that gain spirits (Japanese); keris believed to hold spirits (Malay); The Monkey's Paw (English, 1902)

name: The Voice Inside
beat: Something else speaks through someone you love
roots: The Gerasene demoniac (Gospels); the dybbuk (Ashkenazi Jewish); jinn possession, rasukan (Islamic and Malay folk belief); kitsunetsuki, fox possession (Japanese)

name: The Bargain
beat: Wealth or power bought from something that will collect
roots: Faust (German); pesugihan, wealth pacts with spirits (Javanese); keeping a toyol or polong (Malay); the smith and the devil, ATU 330 (European)

name: The Wrong Child
beat: The child is not what it seems
roots: The changeling (European); the toyol (Malay)

name: The Devouring Mother
beat: The one who should protect is the danger, or grief makes her one
roots: Medea and Lamia (Greek); La Llorona (Mexican)

name: The Double
beat: The self, or someone you love, is replaced or split
roots: Narcissus (Greek); the doppelgänger (German); the fetch (Irish)

name: The Beast Within
beat: A person becomes the animal
roots: Lycaon (Greek, Ovid); harimau jadian, the weretiger (Malay); úlfheðnar wolf-warriors (Norse)

name: The One Who Feeds
beat: The dead or undead live on the living
roots: Penanggalan (Malay); strigoi (Romanian); jiangshi (Chinese); vetala (Indian)

name: The Dead Won't Stay Dead
beat: What was buried returns, wrong
roots: Izanami (Japanese, Kojiki); draugr (Norse); the zombi (Haitian folk belief); pocong (Malay/Indonesian)

name: The Book You Shouldn't Read
beat: Knowledge that destroys the reader
roots: The Book of Thoth in the tale of Setne Khamwas (Egyptian); the tree of knowledge (Hebrew)

name: You Invited It In
beat: The threshold is crossed because someone let it
roots: The vampire must be invited (European folklore); the Trojan horse (Greek); Bloody Mary (folk ritual); Kokkuri-san (Japanese)

name: The Bad Host
beat: Shelter becomes the trap
roots: Polyphemus (Greek, Odyssey); Hansel and Gretel (German); Thyestes' feast (Greek); Baba Yaga's hut (Slavic)

name: The Village Needs Blood
beat: A community buys its survival with someone
roots: Iphigenia (Greek); Jephthah's daughter (Hebrew)

name: The Hunger
beat: An appetite that turns you into the monster
roots: Erysichthon (Greek, Ovid); gaki or preta, the hungry ghosts (Buddhist); the wendigo (Algonquian peoples; handle with care)

name: The Thing Outside
beat: Something hunts the village
roots: Grendel (Old English); the Minotaur (Greek); Yamata no Orochi (Japanese)

name: Stray From the Path
beat: The slasher as cautionary tale: break the rule of the village and be taken
roots: Little Red Riding Hood with Perrault's moral (French, 1697); the warning to be home by maghrib (Malay)

name: The Thing We Made
beat: Our creation turns on us
roots: The Golem of Prague (Jewish); Prometheus and Talos (Greek)

name: The Body Betrays
beat: Transformation from the inside
roots: Ovid's Metamorphoses (Roman); Kafka's Metamorphosis (1915)

name: The Contagion
beat: Horror that spreads person to person
roots: The plagues of Egypt (Hebrew); Apollo's plague, Iliad book 1 (Greek)

name: The Witch at the Edge of the Woods
beat: Power outside the community, feared and sought
roots: Baba Yaga (Slavic); Circe (Greek); Nenek Kebayan (Malay)

name: Nobody Believes Her
beat: She sees it; no one listens
roots: Cassandra and Laocoön (Greek)

name: The Descent
beat: Down into the dark, and something comes back with you
roots: Inanna (Sumerian); Orpheus (Greek); Izanagi (Japanese)

name: The Rule
beat: Survive by one rule: don't look, don't speak, don't move
roots: Medusa (Greek); Orpheus (Greek); Lot's wife (Hebrew); the Crane Wife, Tsuru no Ongaeshi (Japanese)

name: The Endless Night
beat: Trapped in repetition until you change
roots: Sisyphus (Greek); samsara (Hindu/Buddhist)
